title: 17 of the most haunted places in North Wales and their chilling ghost stories
excerpt: Discover 17 supposedly haunted North Wales castles, gaols and historic houses, from Gwrych Castle to Ruthin Gaol, steeped in ghost stories and local folklore.
content:
From centuries-old castles and former prisons to grand country houses, North Wales has no shortage of buildings with a spooky story attached to them.

Some are associated with mysterious figures glimpsed in corridors, while others have tales of unexplained footsteps, voices, doors slamming or objects apparently moving by themselves.

Of course, whether you believe in ghosts is another matter entirely.

Many of the stories have been handed down as folklore or come from paranormal investigators and visitors, rather than being something which can be established as fact.

But with Halloween approaching, we've taken a look at 17 North Wales locations which have developed particularly spooky reputations.

  1. Plas Teg, Pontblyddyn, Flintshire

One of Flintshire's best-known historic houses is also regularly described as one of the area's most haunted.

Paranormal stories surrounding Plas Teg include the so-called Woman in White, as well as accounts of wailing and mysterious apparitions.

One paranormal website goes substantially further, claiming as many as 15 ghosts have been associated with the Jacobean mansion.

  1. Ruthin Gaol, Ruthin

Ruthin Gaol (Image: Submitted)

It is perhaps unsurprising that an old prison should have accumulated a few ghost stories over the years.

Reports surrounding the former gaol include activity associated with the condemned man's cell and doors apparently slamming by themselves.

Other accounts concern the alleged apparition of a former prison guard.

  1. Gwrych Castle, Abergele

Gwrych Castle (Image: Suzanne Kendrick / Newsquest)

The spectacular castle overlooking Abergele frequently crops up in lists of North Wales' supposedly haunted locations.

Among the phenomena claimed at Gwrych Castle are mysterious whispers and alleged poltergeist activity.

Whatever your view of the supernatural, its imposing appearance certainly makes it an atmospheric entry on the list.

  1. Gwydir Castle, Llanrwst

The stories surrounding Gwydir Castle are particularly intriguing because accounts of alleged hauntings are said to stretch back to the 19th century.

One of the best-known tales concerns a young woman associated with the north wing of the property and an area which has become known as the 'Ghost Room'.

  1. Beaumaris Gaol, Anglesey

Beaumaris Gaol (Image: NQ)

Another former prison with a suitably chilling reputation is Beaumaris Gaol.

Visitors are said to have reported footsteps, whispers and shadowy figures.

There is also a tradition surrounding the phantom of a former jailer, whose supposed presence has been linked to unexplained knocking and whistling.

  1. Ruthin Castle Hotel, Ruthin

The Castle Hotel, Ruthin. (Image: Matt Warner)

Perhaps the most famous supernatural tale associated with Ruthin Castle Hotel is that of the Grey Lady.

But she apparently isn't alone.

Other accounts include reported sightings of a soldier and a young girl, alongside stories of unexplained noises and sudden cold spots around the property.

  1. Pen-y-Lan Hall, Ruabon, Wrexham

Pen Y Llan Hall in Ruabon.

Wrexham has several contenders for this list, including Pen-y-Lan Hall near Ruabon.

Paranormal accounts concerning the property include unexplained footsteps and voices.

There are also rather stranger claims of objects apparently disappearing before reappearing, along with alleged sightings associated with children.

  1. Nantclwyd y Dre, Ruthin

(Image: Denbighshire County Council)

The historic timber-framed Nantclwyd y Dre has accumulated several supernatural stories.

Among them is the familiar ghost-story figure of a 'Lady in White'.

Other accounts have involved unexplained scents and shadows apparently moving through the building.

  1. Chirk Castle, Wrexham

Chirk Castle (Image: Newsquest)

One of Wrexham's most recognisable historic landmarks also has its share of paranormal folklore.

Stories connected with Chirk Castle include alleged monk apparitions and reports of mysterious cries.

There have also been claims of figures being spotted in the castle's long gallery.

  1. Penrhyn Old Hall, near Llandudno

Historic Penrhyn Old Hall also appears repeatedly in guides to supposedly haunted locations in North Wales.

Its supernatural reputation has seen it become part of the region's ghost-hunting scene.

  1. Château Rhianfa, Menai Bridge

Château Rhianfa, Menai Bridge (Image: Planning documents)

Château Rhianfa has some of the more unusual stories on our list.

One piece of folklore claims three workmen were buried by a landslide during the building's construction.

There has also been a more recent claim involving a photograph taken during a murder mystery night, in which a mysterious figure was said to have appeared.

Both, however, should be treated as paranormal claims rather than established historical fact.

  1. Plas Mawr, Conwy

The spectacular Elizabethan townhouse in Conwy comes with its own collection of supernatural tales.

Claims surrounding Plas Mawr have included unexplained cold spots and doors apparently slamming.

Perhaps more unusually, paranormal accounts have also referred to a spectral figure described as a doctor.

  1. St Winefride's Well, Holywell

St Winefride's Well, Holywell (Image: Newsquest)

One of Flintshire's most significant historic and religious sites has also attracted a separate strand of paranormal folklore.

Stories associated with St Winefride's Well have included whispers and alleged sightings of shadowy monks and other apparitions.

Those ghost stories are, of course, distinct from the site's religious history and traditions.

  1. Beaumaris Castle, Anglesey

Inside the grounds of Beaumaris Castle. (Image: Newsquest)

The great unfinished medieval fortress is another historic North Wales landmark which has found its way into paranormal guides.

Beaumaris Castle features among locations described as reputedly haunted in the region.

  1. Denbigh Castle, Denbigh

Denbigh Castle (Image: Staff photographer)

There is plenty of folklore attached to Denbigh Castle too.

Claims have included mysterious shadows and the alleged appearance of a boy's face at a window.

Perhaps its most memorable tale, however, concerns a 'White Lady' said to have been spotted around the Goblin Tower.

  1. Bodelwyddan Castle Hotel, Bodelwyddan

Among the reported ghosts at Bodelwyddan Castle Hotel is a figure known as the 'Blue Lady'.

Paranormal accounts have also included shadowy figures, unexplained voices and claims of other unusual physical phenomena.

  1. Conwy Castle, Conwy

Conwy Castle stairwell. (Image: Michael Stenson)

Finally, few locations could provide a more atmospheric setting for a North Wales ghost story than Conwy Castle.

The imposing medieval fortress has appeared in guides to the region's reputedly haunted locations, adding another element of folklore to one of North Wales' best-known landmarks.

Whether ghosts really roam any of these buildings is something readers will have to decide for themselves.

But with ancient castles, former prisons, Jacobean mansions and centuries of stories behind them, North Wales certainly isn't short of places to explore if you're looking for somewhere with a spooky reputation.
